reasoning: The underlying problem (separating benign from sabotage agent trajectories) is well-studied and largely addressed by stronger methods: SHADE-Arena's own LLM monitors reach AUC ~0.87, TRACE reaches F1 0.713/recall 0.844 on SHADE-Arena, and CTRL-ALT-DECEIT reports up to 1.0 AUC on code sabotage. The proposed method — per-token surprisal/entropy from a reference model as an unsupervised threshold/z-score anomaly detector — is a commodity technique: "Detecting Language Model Attacks with Perplexity" (2308.14132), the standard PPL jailbreak baseline, the LessWrong surprisal+entropy OOD post, and especially "Trajectory Anomaly Detection with Language Models" (2409.15366) which already does per-token surprisal-rate thresholding (mean + max-token features, μ+λσ thresholds) for trajectory anomaly detection. What I did NOT find is this exact baseline run on SHADE-Arena benign/sabotage transcripts using an external small (1-3B) reference model with ROC/AUC — existing SHADE-Arena monitoring uses LLM judges, reasoning monitors, and (separately) internal activation probes rather than external reference-model surprise. So the specific baseline-establishing combination is a genuine but narrow gap, while both the problem and the method are heavily covered.

evidence.title: SHADE-Arena: Evaluating Sabotage and Monitoring in LLM Agents
evidence.summary: The benchmark the proposal builds on. Provides labeled benign/sabotage agent trajectories and LLM-monitor baselines (best monitor Gemini 2.5 Pro AUC ~0.87), framing the exact detection problem the proposal targets. Existing monitors are LLM-judge based, not external reference-model surprise.

evidence.title: Trajectory Anomaly Detection with Language Models
evidence.summary: Directly precedes the proposed method: computes per-token surprisal rate from an LM and flags tokens exceeding a data-driven threshold (mu + lambda*sigma), noting aggregate perplexity dilutes anomalies so per-token max-surprisal is better. This is essentially the proposal's feature set and unsupervised thresholding applied to trajectory anomaly detection.

evidence.title: Detecting Language Model Attacks with Perplexity
evidence.summary: Establishes perplexity / negative log-likelihood from a reference model as a training-free unsupervised detector for adversarial/anomalous text, the canonical 'PPL' baseline. Shows the core method is a well-known commodity technique.

evidence.title: TRACE: Trajectory Reasoning through Adaptive Cross-Step Evidence Aggregation for LLM Agents
evidence.summary: State-of-the-art sabotage detector evaluated on ten SHADE-Arena domains (aggregate F1 0.713, recall 0.844). Shows the detection problem on this exact dataset is actively addressed by stronger reasoning-based monitors.

evidence.title: Detecting out of distribution text with surprisal and entropy
evidence.summary: Community work using exactly per-token surprisal and entropy as unsupervised OOD/anomaly signals, including the observation that adversarial tokens are 'surprisingly surprising'. Confirms the surprise+entropy feature approach is established.

evidence.title: Detecting High-Stakes Interactions with Activation Probes
evidence.summary: The cheap-monitor analog: activation probes detect high-stakes/deceptive interactions at ~10^6 fewer FLOPs than LLM monitors. Covers the 'cheap baseline monitor' niche the proposal targets, though via internal activations rather than external reference-model surprise.

evidence.title: CTRL-ALT-DECEIT: Sabotage Evaluations for Automated AI R&D
evidence.summary: Reports LM monitors reaching 0.97-1.0 AUC on code sabotage detection, evidence that the sabotage-detection problem is largely solved by LLM monitors in some settings, weakening the marginal contribution of a weaker statistical baseline.
